question: round5 install task 14 requested timeoutSeconds=1500 (25 min) yet ran 11:17-11:58 (41 min) with no engine-side timeout firing. Is the timeout implementation broken?
method: read candidate deploy service source (matching worktree) + query product DB attempt timeline

sourceFindings.taskLevelContext: deploy_service.go:1597 taskContext, cancelTask := context.WithCancel(context.Background()) -- task-level context has NO deadline, only cancel. A task-level total budget (timeoutSeconds * attempts) does not exist.
sourceFindings.attemptLevelTimeout: deploy_service.go:1708 hostContext, cancelHost := context.WithTimeout(taskContext, deployExecutionTimeout(task)) -- the execution timeout is re-armed per attempt inside executeAsyncHostAttempt, NOT per task.
sourceFindings.retryLoop: deploy_service.go:1690 runAsyncTaskHost() for i := 0; i < deployAttemptMax; i++ { ... } -- up to 3 attempts per host; deployAttemptMax = 3 (deploy_service.go:52).
sourceFindings.scriptExitPropagates: deploySSHClient.RunScript (deploy_service.go:3349) propagates the remote /bin/bash -se exit code; a script-level nonzero exit fails the attempt, then the loop starts the next attempt within milliseconds (no wait).
sourceFindings.cancelReachesSSH: RunScript select on ctx.Done(): closes the client to unblock a pending channel-open, then <-done; a fired attempt deadline DOES return context deadline exceeded (the 20s timeout case reproduced it).

dbEvidence.attemptSpacing: each attempt boundary gap ~50ms (BACKOFF none) -> the 3 attempts are contiguous retries, all by the same worker deploy-worker:1795403825794053500

triage.conclusion: NOT a broken timeout. No attempt ever consumed its full 25-min budget: each attempt ended at ~15 min wall-clock with script-level 'Process exited with status 28' (consistent with 3 x curl --max-time 300 inside the template script). The 41-min wall clock = 3 contiguous attempts x ~15 min, not a single 25-min budget being ignored. A truly stuck script WOULD fire context deadline exceeded at 25 min (the round-2 20s timeout case proves the propagation path).

gap.semantic: timeoutSeconds=1500 is presented as the task's execution timeout (UI/API field ExecutionTimeoutSeconds) but the implementation treats it as PER-ATTEMPT budget, multiplied by up to deployAttemptMax(3) attempts = effective 75 min ceiling. A user setting 25 min gets up to ~75 min of wall-clock only when every attempt fails late.
gap.only_visible_when: script fails slowly enough that each attempt approaches its own budget (3x curl at 5 min each here).
gap.not_visible_when: normal success (attempt 1 finishes fast), or a hard hang (first attempt fires at budget, then loop retries).

ruler_options_for_maintainer: A. Accept per-attempt semantics: document that ExecutionTimeoutSeconds is the per-attempt budget and retries multiply it; no code change.

B. Task-level total budget: wrap taskContext with context.WithTimeout(totalBudget) so the whole retry loop shares one deadline. Minimal, but changes existing retry behavior and needs its own acceptance.
C. Cap retry window: derive total = timeoutSeconds * deployAttemptMax and document; small code, closes the surprise but keeps per-attempt semantics.
triage.recommendation: Option A or C. The timeout path itself is proved working; do not classify as a bug/defect. This is a T02 Known-Gap closure item pending maintainer ruling (gate-policy touchpoint).
